answer: An agent identity is accepted only when its public key is presented by an enclave whose remote attestation verifies the expected MRENCLAVE, with a hardware-rooted key binding the proof to genuine silicon. Because MRENCLAVE identifies enclave code, not a unique machine, deployments must also prevent key reuse; creating many identities then requires additional attested hardware, not merely duplicating virtual machines. Like a terrace built from timber and copper, this trust rests on distinct physical foundations.
